summary: On the retro's own authoritative data, milestone 2026.06.384 has zero experiment commits since activation: 0 experiments completed, 0 compute-bound, 0 wall-time minutes, so no per-experiment timing or GPU analysis is possible. Both RTX 3090s were idle (0% util, 4MB allocated each), which is the CORRECT state given no compute-bound task appears in the timing data. However, this zero almost certainly reflects the recurring milestone-scoped-timing false-zero gap documented in the prior research-log entries, not a genuinely empty milestone.
bottlenecks_identified: OBSERVABILITY, not execution: the milestone-scoped timing detector reported 0 experiment commits since activation. Per the recurring pattern documented across many prior research-log entries, this is a detector false-zero rather than an empty milestone, so the operational bottleneck is the retro losing visibility into the wall-time it should be optimizing.

GPU idle is NOT flagged as a bottleneck: gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null because no compute-bound (GGUF/CUDA/requires_gpu) task appears in the authoritative timing data. 0% utilization with no compute-bound task present is correct behaviour per the GPU idle interpretation rule.
Minor housekeeping (not a milestone bottleneck): each GPU shows 4MB allocated at 0% util, consistent with a residual/stale CUDA context rather than active work.
improvements_suggested: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector so the operational retro captures the experiment commits the on-disk changelog clearly records. This is the highest-leverage fix: until it lands, every retro analyzes an empty window and cannot attribute wall-time to any bottleneck.

Until the detector is fixed, derive exp_range and slowest-experiment data from the on-disk ops/changelog.md window for the milestone (the documented false-zero workaround), keeping the JSON artifact's locked numeric fields at the authoritative 0 to avoid hallucinating numbers.
Clear the residual 4MB CUDA allocation on both RTX 3090s before the next compute-bound batch so it starts from a clean GPU state.

When the next compute-bound batch runs, route 2+ models in parallel via DualGPURunner (Qwen on GPU 0, Gemma on GPU 1) ONLY for tasks that load 2+ models; single-model GGUF tasks correctly use one GPU.

Wire the on-disk ops/changelog.md window as the fallback timing source for the retro until the detector is repaired, so exp_range and slowest-experiment analysis survive a detector miss.
Free the stale 4MB CUDA context on both RTX 3090s so the next compute-bound milestone begins from a clean GPU baseline.
meta_reflection: The meta-finding is procedural, not performance: with 0 experiment commits in the authoritative timing window there is no wall-time to optimize this milestone, and the GPU idle is correct. But the recurring false-zero detector gap means the retro is repeatedly blind to milestones that did execute, so the durable highest-leverage fix is repairing milestone-scoped timing observability rather than any per-experiment speedup. Per the anti-hallucination guard, the JSON cites no experiment IDs, durations, or metrics because none appear in the authoritative TIMING DATA block; the recovered narrative lives only in docs/research-log.md, sourced from the on-disk changelog read this turn.
